material.text: opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy: OpenCode plugin (V1 + V2) that converts raw tool-call markup from local Ollama models into standard OpenAI tool_calls, plus line-ending normalization for file edits.

type=plugin source=npm:opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy created=2026-07-13T23:08:09.744Z firstSeen=2026-11-01T21:11:48.277Z published=2026-11-16T23:24:07.212Z maintainers=mareksagan repoId=? stars=? npm30d=?

# OpenCode Ollama Tool-Call Proxy Plugin An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that does two things: 1. **Tool-call conversion**: intercepts chat-completion responses from a local [Ollama](https://ollama.com) server and rewrites raw tool-call markup into standard OpenAI `tool_calls` chunks. This lets models that do not expose native Ollama tool support still work as agentic coding models inside OpenCode. 2. **Line-ending normalization**: normalizes LF/CRLF line endings on `write`, `edit`, and `multiedit` tool arguments, and on files after edits, using `.editorconfig` or the `OPENCODE_LINE_ENDINGS` environment variable. Platform default: CRLF on Windows, LF on Linux/macOS. One package version supports both major OpenCode lines: **V2** loads the plugin through the native `setup()` API (including the `http.response` session hook for response rewriting), while **V1** (≥ 1.18.29) uses the `server()` entry point with a global fetch interceptor. ## Supported model families | Family | Example Ollama tags | Raw markup handled | |--------|---------------------|--------------------| | Qwen 2.5 / Qwen 2.5-Coder | `qwen2.5-coder`, `qwen2.5` | ``, ``, raw JSON object/array | | Qwen 3.5 / Qwen 3-Coder | `qwen3.5`, `qwen3-coder` | `{...}` and `` XML | | Ornith 1.0 | `ornith-9b`, `ornith-35b` | same as Qwen 3.5 (routed to Qwen converter) | | Gemma 4 | `gemma4` | <|tool_call>call:name{...}<tool_call|>, `...` | | Mistral / Ministral | `mistral`, `mistral-nemo`, `ministral`, `ministral-3` | `[TOOL_CALLS] JSON array` and `[ARGS]{...}` | | Llama 3.x / OpenCoder | `llama3.1`, `llama3.2`, `llama3.3`, `opencoder` | raw JSON object/array, <|python_tag>...<|eom_id|> | | Phi-4 / Phi-4 Tools | `phi4-mini`, `phi4-tools` | `{"name":..., "parameters":...}`, `functools[...]` | | DeepSeek R1 / V3 | `deepseek-r1`, `deepseek-v3` | `<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>` tags, fenced JSON, raw JSON, strips `` | | Yi-Coder | `yi-coder` | raw JSON / JSON array, code fences | | GLM-4 / ChatGLM | `glm4`, `chatglm3` | `[TOOL_REQUEST] {...} [END_TOOL_REQUEST]`, legacy `` XML | | Laguna XS 2.1 | `laguna-xs-2.1` | `[tool=name]`, `[tool=namekv]` | ## Installation ### OpenCode V2 From npm: ```bash npm install -g opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy ``` Then add the package name to the `plugins` array in `opencode.json`: ```json { "plugins": ["opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy"] } ``` From a local checkout: ```bash git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USER/opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy.git npm install npm run build ``` V2 loads local plugins by **directory** (not by `.js` file — file paths are skipped with a warning). Point `plugins` at the package root, which exposes `dist/index.js` through `package.json` `exports`: ```json { "plugins": ["file:///C:/absolute/path/to/opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy"] } ``` Restart OpenCode. The plugin is loaded automatically. ### OpenCode V1 (legacy, ≥ 1.18.29) V1 keeps using the `plugin` key and the `server()` entry point. From npm, same install plus: ```json { "plugin": ["opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy"] } ``` From a local checkout, reference the built entry point with an absolute `file://` URL (V1 loads files, V2 loads directories): ```json { "plugin": ["file:///C:/absolute/path/to/opencode-ollama-toolcall-proxy/dist/index.js"] } ``` ## Usage 1. Make sure Ollama is running. 2. Configure your model in `opencode.json` with tool support enabled. ### OpenCode V2 Use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/v1`) so chat-completion traffic flows through the `http.response` hook, and mark the model as tool-capable with `capabilities`: ```json { "providers": { "ollama": { "package": "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "settings": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:11434/v1" }, "models": { "qwen2.5-coder:14b": { "name": "Qwen2.5 Coder 14B", "capabilities": { "tools": true } } } } } } ``` > V2 auto-discovers Ollama at `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, but the plugin converts responses on the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` route. Configure the provider explicitly as shown so requests use that route. ### OpenCode V1 (legacy) ```json { "provider": { "ollama": { "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "options": { "baseURL": "http://localhost:11434/v1" }, "models": { "qwen2.5-coder:14b": { "name": "Qwen2.5 Coder 14B", "tools": true, "thinking": false } } } } } ``` 3. Start OpenCode. When the model emits raw tool-call text, the plugin converts it to proper `tool_calls` before the AI SDK sees the response. Note on tool argument shapes: V2 tools address files with `path`, V1 tools with `filePath`; the plugin handles both automatically. The `multiedit` tool exists on V1 only — on V2 it is simply unused. ## Line-ending configuration The plugin normalizes line endings on file writes/edits in this priority order: 1. `OPENCODE_LINE_ENDINGS` environment variable (`lf` or `crlf`) 2. `.editorconfig` `end_of_line` setting (walks up the directory tree) 3. Platform default: `crlf` on Windows, `lf` on Linux/macOS Example `.editorconfig`: ```ini root = true [*] end_of_line = crlf [*.sh] end_of_line = lf ``` Binary files (images, archives, fonts, media, etc.) are never rewritten. ## Debug logging Debug logging is **off by default**. Set `LLM_PROXY_DEBUG=1` to append plugin diagnostics (including model-output snippets) to `LLM_PROXY_LOG`, or to `/tmp/opencode-proxy-debug.log` (or `~/opencode-proxy-debug.log` on Windows) when `LLM_PROXY_LOG` is unset. ## Development ```bash # type check npm run typecheck # run tests npm test # build a single ESM bundle for publishing npm run build ``` Live tests against a real Ollama instance (`node --experimental-strip-types real-test.ts [model]`, `real-stream-test.ts`) exercise the V1 fetch interceptor end to end. ## Publishing 1. Pick a unique npm package name and update `name` in `package.json`. 2. Log in to npm: `npm login`. 3. Publish: `npm publish`. The `prepublishOnly` script automatically builds `dist/index.js` before the package is uploaded. ## License MIT
